groups.sentence: Instructors set clear course AI policies that follow institutional principles, including a syllabus statement.
The university publishes baseline principles and a shared framework for AI use in teaching and learning.
Certain core expectations for AI use apply in every course.
The university supports and is committed to responsible, ethical exploration and use of AI.
The university aims to use AI to advance its mission, innovation, teaching, research and student preparation.
Core principles and concerns for AI use include integrity, privacy, security, fairness, copyright and values.
Everyone uses AI responsibly and ethically, in line with university values, fairness, privacy, academic integrity and policy principles.
Students use AI tools responsibly and ethically.
AI is human-centered and supports, rather than replaces, human judgment, relationships, critical thinking and teaching.
This framework states the purpose and scope of university AI guidance and affirms shared community values.
AI brings both opportunities and risks, requiring a balance of innovation against integrity and learning.
Transparency and honest communication about AI use are expected and essential.
Everyone protects data, privacy and security and complies with applicable laws when using AI.
The university deploys and governs AI to serve its values, such as equity and autonomy, in proportion to risk.
Everyone does not use AI in ways that undermine learning objectives, assessment integrity or evaluation of student work.
Users are accountable for the AI outputs they generate or rely on and account for AI's limitations.
Instructors use AI to support learning outcomes and balance academic integrity with its benefits, prioritizing human agency.
